title: Packings in real Grassmannian spaces: N n-dimensional subspaces of R^m with the largest least squared chordal distance
keeper: N. J. A. Sloane, Table of best Grassmannian packings (with R. H. Hardin, J. H. Conway and others)
revision: grassTab.html as served on 15 Nov 2026 (last modified 20 Jan 1997)

template.title: Grassmannian packing: {N} subspaces of dimension {n} in R^{m}
template.statement: Find {N} subspaces of dimension {n} of R^{m} whose least squared chordal distance is as large as possible. The squared chordal distance of two subspaces is the sum of the squares of the sines of their {n} principal angles, {n} - tr(P_A P_B) for their orthogonal projections (Conway, Hardin and Sloane, 1996).
template.submission: Text file: {N} x {n} x {m} numbers (integers, decimals or fractions p/q), the {n} spanning vectors of {m} coordinates of each subspace one after the other, as in Sloane's files (neilsloane.com/grass/dim{m}/); the vectors need not be orthonormal. See checkers/grass_check.py.

score: the least squared chordal distance between two of the subspaces, exact (larger is better)
best_text: The best known value is {best} ({holder}); the table prints its values rounded, so a packing improves it when its least squared chordal distance is larger by more than one unit in the last printed decimal.
bound_source: Rankin's simplex bound n(m-n)/m N/(N-1), and for N > m(m+1)/2 the orthoplex bound n(m-n)/m (Conway, Hardin and Sloane 1996)
holder_unknown: the table's source for the entry
holder_sources: the name column of the table (Hardin and Sloane's computer searches, or the paper of a construction); later packings from families/grassmannian-packing/literature.json
open_rule: every (m, n, N) of the table whose best known value (the largest the table lists for N or more subspaces, or a later published packing) is below the bound by more than one unit of its last printed decimal, unless optimality has been proven since (literature.json)
left_out: 2826 rows; 5 rows above the bound (not used); 2778 (m, n, N) in the table; 434 equal to the bound (solved); 8 proven optimal since 1997 (solved); 14 exact forms of the table's own packings (Fickus, Jasper and Mixon); 97 too large to check; 11 raised by Fickus, Jasper and Mixon (2018)
